story.fullStory:
Dixie Chicks's "Goodbye Earl" reached #19 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Goodbye Earl" is a country murder ballad written by Dennis Linde.

Initially recorded by the band Sons of the Desert for an unreleased album in the late 1990s, the song gained fame when it was recorded by Dixie Chicks on their fifth studio album, Fly.

After charting from unsolicited airplay in late 1999, the song was released as that album's third single in 2000, peaking at No.

The song peaked at #19 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 15 weeks on the chart.
